solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Fool cancelled radical playwright (7)

blocks.note: a berk is a fool (British slang)
a match that is off has been cancelled

annotation.surface: A radical playwright is dismissed as a fool whose show has been cancelled.
annotation.walkthrough: Steven Berkoff is the British actor-playwright known for his confrontational, physical theatre. BERK is British slang for an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: Berkoff's stylised, aggressive plays made him the radical of the British stage.

entries.clue: Raccoon’s been shot south of British national park (6,7)

indicatorNotes.shot: something shot is ruined, so the letters come out wrecked and rearranged
indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, south of a letter means written below it, so the rearranged letters come after B

blocks.note: the twelve letters of RACCOONS BEEN rearranged
places the rearranged letters below B

annotation.surface: A hunter reports that a raccoon has been shot somewhere south of a British national park.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' reads as gunfire but means the letters are wrecked. The Brecon Beacons are mountains in south Wales.
annotation.definitionFit: The Beacons in south Wales were designated one of Britain's national parks in 1957.

entries.clue: Intend to wear ripped clothing (7)

indicatorNotes.to wear: a word that wears another has it on, wrapped around it like a coat

blocks.note: the torn word goes on around the intention

annotation.surface: Someone means to go out in torn clothes.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'to wear' and 'clothing' side by side so the whole clue seems to be about dressing; only 'clothing' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An old, literary word for garments, found mostly in the Bible and poetry.

entries.clue: Group table depleted in a month (5)

indicatorNotes.depleted: a depleted word has had its contents used up, leaving only its shell
indicatorNotes.in: the emptied table sits inside the month

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
TABLE emptied of its middle leaves T…E

annotation.surface: A group finds the table empty during a certain month.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depleted' means the word loses all its contents, not just a letter or two; only the outer letters of TABLE survive.
annotation.definitionFit: A set of eight performers or things is one kind of group.

entries.clue: At first, factoids and numbers suit organised admirers (3,5)

indicatorNotes.At first: taking each word at its first means reading only its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letters of Factoids And Numbers
clubs is one of the four card suits

annotation.surface: Trivia and statistics appeal to an organised body of enthusiasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suit' reads as a verb, as in 'factoids suit admirers', but it is the noun: a suit of cards.
annotation.definitionFit: Admirers of a star who form a society with membership and newsletters are organised.

entries.clue: Court order briefly introduced to silence chatterbox (6)

indicatorNotes.briefly: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.introduced to: something introduced to a thing is put into it

blocks.note: ASBO, an anti-social behaviour order, cut short

annotation.surface: A judge issues a court order to shut up someone who talks too much.
annotation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order restraining nuisance behaviour. The surface makes the order the thing that silences; in the wordplay it is the part slipped inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for someone who talks too much, the first suggesting hot air.

entries.clue: Male races in run for lowly quarter? (6)

indicatorNotes.in: the man and the races go inside the word for run

blocks.note: to go is to run, as a machine does
the TT races on the Isle of Man

annotation.surface: A man runs races in search of a cheap part of town.
annotation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is the Isle of Man motorcycle race meeting, a crossword staple for 'races'.
annotation.definitionFit: A poor, segregated district of a city is a quarter of low standing.

entries.clue: Hairy beast crouching in small out-of-bounds dacha (9)

indicatorNotes.out-of-bounds: a word put out of its bounds loses its boundary letters, first and last
indicatorNotes.in: the crouching word goes inside what is left of the dacha

blocks.note: DACHA with its bounds (first and last letters) removed

annotation.surface: A hairy beast crouches inside a little Russian country house it should not be in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-bounds' reads as forbidden, but it strips the boundary letters from DACHA. A dacha is a Russian country cottage.
annotation.definitionFit: Also called Bigfoot, the ape-man of North American legend is covered in hair.

entries.clue: French city soon collects six grand (7)

indicatorNotes.collects: a word that collects others gathers them up and holds them inside

annotation.surface: A French city will soon receive six thousand pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grand' reads as an adjective describing the city, but it is slang for a thousand, abbreviated G.
annotation.definitionFit: The Provençal city on the Rhône was the seat of the popes in the 14th century.

entries.clue: Being sixteen, boisterous and extremely carefree (9)

indicatorNotes.boisterous: boisterous means rowdy and unruly, so the letters will not stay in line
indicatorNotes.extremely: taken at its extremes, a word gives only its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A portrait of being a rowdy, carefree sixteen-year-old.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' looks like the start of a sentence about a teenager; it is the definition, as a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: As a noun, being is the plain synonym: the state of being alive or real.

entries.clue: Superficially deals with captains (5)

blocks.note: to skip a topic is to pass over it lightly
skip = skipper, the captain of a team or boat

annotation.surface: Someone treats their leaders with only surface attention.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Captains' reads as a noun being dealt with; it is a second definition in its own right.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb means passing lightly over a subject; the noun is short for skippers, team captains in curling and bowls.

entries.clue: Selected MPs secretly follow case surrounding TV (6,7)

blocks.note: to shadow someone is to tail them unseen
the wooden cabinet that old television sets were built into

annotation.surface: Chosen MPs are being tailed, perhaps by someone watching a TV case.
annotation.walkthrough: The shadow cabinet is the team of opposition MPs who each mirror a government minister; the leader selects them.
annotation.definitionFit: The opposition leader picks a team of MPs to mirror the ministers, so they are selected.

entries.clue: Public secret initially suppressed (5)

indicatorNotes.initially suppressed: a word whose initial is suppressed has its first letter held back

blocks.note: the first letter, C, is removed

annotation.surface: A secret that was stifled at first has come into public view.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition and the word being trimmed are opposites, which is the pleasure of the clue: one letter turns a secret into its opposite.
annotation.definitionFit: Done openly rather than hidden, so public, a plain synonym.

entries.clue: First couple from Hungary trapped in rioting Italian republic (9)

indicatorNotes.First couple from: the first couple of letters from a word are its first two
indicatorNotes.trapped in: the two letters are caught inside the rearranged word
indicatorNotes.rioting: rioting means running wild, so the letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the first two letters of HUngary

annotation.surface: Two Hungarians are caught up in an Italian riot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Italian republic' reads as one phrase, but 'Italian' belongs to the wordplay and 'republic' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Baltic state has been an independent republic since 1990, a definition by example.

entries.clue: Die in hot water? (8)

blocks.note: not the verb for dying but the noun: a die is a cube
not in trouble but literally in a hot bath

annotation.surface: Someone meets their end in trouble, or in scalding water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Die' reads as a verb about death; it is the noun, a dice cube. A bath cube is a scented block that dissolves in bathwater.
annotation.definitionFit: A scented block of bath salts is cube-shaped like a die and is dropped into a hot bath.

entries.clue: Old county Conservative getting even afterwards (9)

blocks.note: and = and then, afterwards, as in 'he ate and left'

annotation.surface: A Tory in an old county finally settles the score.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting even' reads as revenge, but 'even' alone is LEVEL, and 'getting' only joins it to the Conservative.
annotation.definitionFit: The county around Middlesbrough existed only from 1974 to 1996, so it is an old one.

entries.clue: Drunken idiots rolling over floor (6)

indicatorNotes.rolling over: something rolling over turns upside down, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to floor someone is to knock them out, KO

annotation.surface: Drunk fools are tumbling about on the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is exactly the scene of the answer, drunks on the floor, and 'floor' is a verb in the wordplay: to knock down.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang synonym for very drunk.

entries.clue: Jockey announced “great success” after losing round in sporting event (5,3)

indicatorNotes.announced: something announced is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the jockey
indicatorNotes.after losing round: round is the letter O, the shape of a circle, and it is lost

blocks.note: a jockey is a rider; the name is spelt differently
COUP, a great success, without the letter O

annotation.surface: A jockey declares a triumph at a sporting event.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ryder Cup is the golf contest between Europe and the USA. 'Round' is the letter O, shaped like a circle.
annotation.definitionFit: The biennial Europe-versus-USA golf tournament is a sporting event, a definition by example.

entries.clue: Flier takes part in viva voce tests (6)

indicatorNotes.takes part in: the answer is a part taken from inside the following words

annotation.surface: An aviator sits oral examinations.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot sitting exams; it is a bird. The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill.
annotation.definitionFit: A black-and-white wading bird, so a flier by example; a viva voce is an oral exam.

entries.clue: Public company starts to manufacture excellent product (7)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of the following words are their first letters

blocks.note: once news is out, it is public
the first letters of Manufacture and Excellent

annotation.surface: A listed company begins making a first-rate product.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Public company' reads as one business term from the stock market, and 'product' as goods off a line; both split apart here.
annotation.definitionFit: A product in the sense of a result, what something yields.

entries.clue: Snake-like, unusually hypnotic (8)

indicatorNotes.unusually: done unusually, the letters are not in their usual order

annotation.surface: Something snake-like and strangely mesmerising, like Kaa in The Jungle Book.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits the answer: snakes are famed for hypnotising their prey.
annotation.definitionFit: Formed from the name of a big constrictor, it means resembling that snake.

entries.clue: Report of bad general situation for molluscs (7)

indicatorNotes.Report of: a report is something spoken, so the answer sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: naughty = bad, and the lie of the land is the general situation

annotation.surface: A news report describes a bad situation for shellfish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lie' here is the lie of the land, the general layout of things. The plural is Latin, with -I.
annotation.definitionFit: Spiral-shelled sea creatures related to squid are cephalopod molluscs.

entries.clue: Radio astronomer’s source of celestial observations early in year? (6)

blocks.note: January comes early in the year
the sky is where stars are observed

annotation.surface: A radio astronomer's January sky watching.
annotation.walkthrough: Karl Jansky was the American engineer who founded radio astronomy; the unit of radio flux is named after him. The clue half-says 'Jan's sky'.
annotation.definitionFit: Karl Jansky first detected radio waves from the Milky Way in the 1930s.

entries.clue: Goethe upset with man working as a solicitor? (2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall out of order

annotation.surface: The German poet is annoyed with a man who works as a lawyer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests an English lawyer, but here it is someone soliciting in the street. The answer is British slang for working as a prostitute.
annotation.definitionFit: A prostitute solicits for clients, so the question mark flags a solicitor of an unlegal sort.

entries.clue: Uncovered disparagements in, say, King’s promotional description (5)

indicatorNotes.Uncovered: a word uncovered has its covering stripped off, its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.in: the stripped word goes inside the king's initials

blocks.note: B.B. King, the blues guitarist; 'say' marks him as one example of a King
SLURS with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: Insults about a monarch are exposed in some advertising copy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'King' looks like royalty; it is the bluesman B.B. King. 'Uncovered' strips the covering letters from SLURS.
annotation.definitionFit: The short puff on a book jacket is a promotional description.

entries.clue: One way to join equid when cycling (5)

indicatorNotes.when cycling: letters cycling go round like a wheel, the front ones coming round to the back

blocks.note: the zebra is a member of the horse family, Equidae
the first two letters travel round to the end

annotation.surface: A way to link up with a horse while out on a bike.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' reads as riding a bicycle; it means letters wheeling round from one end to the other.
annotation.definitionFit: Soldering metal with a brass alloy is one method of joining.

entries.clue: Car manufacturer endorses backing Russian agreement (5)

indicatorNotes.backing: backing a word runs it in reverse, like a car

blocks.note: to OK something is to endorse it

annotation.surface: A carmaker supports a deal with Russia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as supporting, which is what 'endorses' already means; here it turns the endorsement round.
annotation.definitionFit: The Czech carmaker, now part of Volkswagen, is a definition by example.

entries.clue: Narrow-minded Jack stops fighting in case (9)

indicatorNotes.stops: the sailor stops a gap, plugging himself into the middle of the other letters
indicatorNotes.fighting: letters fighting are thrown about in a scuffle

blocks.note: a jack tar is a sailor

annotation.surface: A bigoted man called Jack breaks up a fight, just in case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' reads as a phrase meaning 'as a precaution', but it is six letters of fodder. Jack and TAR both mean a sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: Bigoted in favour of one's own sect or faction, hence narrow-minded.

entries.clue: Bloom’s colour about to be hidden by grass (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about means turned round, as in about-face
indicatorNotes.to be hidden by: a word hidden by another is tucked away inside it

annotation.surface: A flower's colour is about to vanish in the long grass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloom' looks like a flower, and 'about to' like 'soon going to'; 'about' alone is the reversal, and 'Bloom' is the prime of life.
annotation.definitionFit: In full bloom means at one's peak, and the answer is that prime time.

entries.clue: Foretell old Brit will consume wine (7)

indicatorNotes.will consume: the old Brit drinks the wine down, so it ends up inside him

blocks.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland

annotation.surface: A prophecy that an ancient Briton will drink some wine.
annotation.walkthrough: PICT for 'old Brit' is a crossword regular: the Picts lived in what is now Scotland before the Scots.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to say what will happen before it does.
